name: Rust Safety
description: Enforces safe Rust patterns with proper error handling and minimal unsafe usage.
content:
# Rust Safety Rules

- Never use `unsafe` blocks without a `// SAFETY:` comment explaining the invariant
- Use `Result<T, E>` for recoverable errors — avoid `unwrap()` and `expect()` in production code
- Prefer `Option<T>` over sentinel values for optional data
- Derive `Debug` on all public types for better error messages
- Use `thiserror` for library error types and `anyhow` for application error types
- Prefer `&str` over `String` in function parameters when ownership isn't needed
- Use `clippy` lints at warn level minimum — `#![warn(clippy::all)]`
- Prefer iterators and combinators over manual index-based loops
- Use `Arc<Mutex<T>>` for shared mutable state — document the locking strategy
- Keep `pub` visibility minimal — expose only what's part of the API
